items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names reveal intent (`queue_iter`, `worker`, `errors`, `factory`). The docstring explains the cancellation and error behaviour, and the cleanup retry loop has a comment explaining it.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One function of about 55 lines with a nested worker and a hand-written retry loop (`while True: ... gather ... cancel`) where TaskGroup would do. The post-wait `w.exception()` check is nearly dead code, since workers already catch every `Exception`.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Rejects bad input (`ValueError` for `max_concurrent < 1`) and cleans up carefully on cancel. But `except BaseException:` is a catch-all, and only `raise errors[0]` is surfaced, so every later task exception is silently dropped.

items.name: Failures and degenerate arguments
items.evidence: An empty list returns at once and `max_concurrent < 1` raises `ValueError`. When a task raises, the others are not cancelled and queued tasks still start (`except Exception: errors.append(exc)`). The error surfaces only at the end. Nothing leaks or hangs.

items.name: Required signature and import behaviour
items.name_zh: 签名与导入行为符合要求
items.evidence: `async def run_tasks(tasks: list[Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]], max_concurrent: int) -> None`. Workers call each factory lazily, only when a slot is free. Stdlib only, nothing runs at import.
